The '''2004 World Championship''' was the 9th Star Wars CCG World Championship, run by the [[Players Committee]] at Gen Con in Indianapolis, Indiana, on 19–22 August 2004.<ref name="tfn-2004">[https://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/Star_Wars_CCG_2004_World_Championships_to_be_at_GenCon_83658.asp Star Wars CCG 2004 World Championships to be at GenCon], TheForce.Net (6 May 2004): "held at this year's GenCon in Indianapolis, Indiana, August 19-22"</ref><ref name="awards">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/community/awards/ Awards and Hall of Fame], starwarsccg.org; Wayback [https://web.archive.org/web/20230817222457/https://www.starwarsccg.org/community/awards/ 17 August 2023]</ref><ref name="pc-2004">[http://www.swccgpc.com/interior.htm SWCCGPC.com] (World Championship at Gen Con Indy, 19–22 August 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040710155145/http://www.swccgpc.com/interior.htm Internet Archive, 10 July 2004]</ref> [[Brandon Schele]] defeated [[Reid Smith]] in the final.<ref name="awards" /> Schele posted his Dark [[My Lord, Is That Legal? / I Will Make It Legal|My Lord, Is That Legal?]] and Light [[Yavin 4: Massassi Throne Room]] decks on DeckTech as his "World Champion" lists (see Results). The Players Committee held all three days in the DecipherCon area of Gen Con at the Indiana Convention Center; Day 3 was a top-12 cut, and the winner received $1,000.<ref name="pc-gencon04" /> [[Greg Anderson]] was the listed tournament director<ref name="pc-events0406">[https://web.archive.org/web/20040604012322/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/events.htm Events (2004)], swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 4 June 2004.</ref> and, as the only Advocate present, ran all three days.<ref name="pcf-4063">[https://web.archive.org/web/20041216005232/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?t=4063&amp State of the PC Address: So long and thanks for all the fish], David Kangas (25 October 2004), with reply by Brandon Schele, Player's Committee Forums, swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 16 December 2004.</ref> The field size and the final places from 3rd down have not been found.

The constructed pool was printed Decipher cards through [[Theed Palace]] plus the original [[Virtual Sets (2002-2009)|Players Committee Virtual Sets]] then legal. The wiki files it under [[Premiere - Original VS6]], from the newest virtual cards in the published lists; a numbered cutoff for the event has not been confirmed.

Places from 3rd down are not known; a 2020 forum thread that compiled Worlds Day 3 results also lists places 3–8 as missing. The Players Committee's schedule advanced the top 12 from Day 2 to Day 3,<ref name="pc-gencon04" /> so Day 3 had more than eight players. In an October 2004 forum post [[David Kangas]] wrote that [[Nick Jones]] "placed first in Day 2" and that the Day 3 setup put him "in the money regardless of how you played"; in a reply, Schele wrote that he played [[Lee Edwards]] in the first round of Day 3.<ref name="pcf-4063" /><ref name="f75427">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?t=75427 SWCCG Worlds Day 3 Standings History], forum.starwarsccg.org (thread, May 2020 onward). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261012152200/https://swccg.com/snapshots/forum/t75427.html Internet Archive]</ref> Decks are the lists recovered in 2026 from DeckTech posts (Internet Archive copies) and Players Committee decklist forms; each deck page cites its own source.

=== Day 3 bracket ===

Not published in the sources found.

=== Schedule and prizes ===

The Players Committee's Gen Con 2004 schedule (TD [[Greg Anderson]]):<ref name="pc-gencon04" /><ref name="pc-events0406" />

* Thursday 19 August: Day 1 Heat 1 at noon and Heat 2 at 6 PM ($20 each; top 25% advance to Day 2).
* Friday 20 August: 10 AM Day 2 (free; "Top 12 Advance to Day 3, Prizes for all").
* Saturday 21 August: 10 AM Day 3 (free; "$1000 1st place, Cash to top places").

The same schedule listed a Classic constructed event and a Secret Squirrel sealed deck event, the Gen Con Team Tournament, and the Jedi Knights (Friday 3 PM) and Young Jedi (Saturday 1 PM) World Championships, each with $100 to the winner.<ref name="pc-gencon04" />
